text: The stop-gate judge's class-sweep/proof check fires on a transform that is still IN FLIGHT in a leased writer (the 47-alias conversion, writer a023840, #d143cbdd): nothing has landed, yet it demands shape proof for a 'landed' bulk transform. A class-sweep or proof obligation should key on a TICKED item or a committed diff, not on an open lease's description; the owed proof belongs in the writer's tick evidence, which the lead has already required (class count 77 vs 47, shape_cluster_diff, per-package tsc/tests).

An interim SubagentStop from an agent that is still waiting on its own background task (text like 'waiting for the background test run', 'I'll wait for this notification') is captured as a [SILENT]/unread report and blocks the lead's stop every time, although it carries nothing to act on. P1.5 auto-read excludes [SILENT] on purpose; an interim-wait report whose agent is still live (a running background child) should be auto-read or held until the agent's final stop.

A submodule pointer 'move' in the shared tree can be the tree LAGGING the babysitter's snapshot commits (tree HEAD older than the recorded gitlink, with uncommitted work on top), not an intended move; neither 'stage it' nor 'git submodule update --checkout' is right then -- the next combined submodule commit resolves it. Check: git diff --cached shows nothing for the path and the recorded commit is a descendant of the tree HEAD.

The tick evidence check refuses a sha from a sibling (non-submodule) repo such as private/generative or private/growth: it resolves shas only in the console repo. Use the remote's commit URL as evidence, or teach the check to try git -C <each private/* repo>.

After TaskStop on a writer agent, the pre-agent cap guard can still count it as live (its transcript never shows end_turn); the slot stays blocked until another writer finishes. Check the roster with the guard's own listing before assuming a free slot.

the plan-adopted recipe wraps box text in double quotes while the text itself opens with (" -- copying it verbatim is a bash syntax error; the suggested --add must shell-quote its argument (shlex.quote). Fold into PLAN-stop-hook-one-plan-scope.

plan-unimplemented still enforces the descending all-plans ceiling (315 vs 68) that CI dropped on 2026-09-26 and that the operator's 2026-10-03 'PR plan + loop only' ruling scopes to the PR's plan; a reconciliation writer already working door 1 cannot quiet it within a stop. Fixed by PLAN-stop-hook-one-plan-scope SC6; until then it should downgrade to an advisory while a writer leased to plan reconciliation is live.

A background wait loop inherits the shell cwd at launch, so relative paths in it silently point elsewhere after a cd into a submodule: a pre-push waited 12 min on agent/reviews/... under private/account. Start every background command with cd <abs> or use absolute paths

The stop-gate judge can return verdict=not-legitimate while its own reason says the stop IS legitimate (2026-10-05: six live workers, wake timer armed, reason "pure background wait is legitimate", next action "await worker output"); the verdict field must be checked against the reason, or the judge asked for a single boolean the reason cannot contradict
Lease a background task only by the id its own launch result printed; picking "the newest file in the tasks dir" grabbed the wake timer or another task three times on 2026-10-05

An edit to a file a generated doc region reads (.ci/policy/*, .ci/config/env-manifest.json, gates.lock.json) is not done until npx tsx scripts/gen/gen-docs.ts runs clean; 1006-1 missed it twice (423397221, 84cfe4e55) and each miss cost a 17 min pre-push
A read-only investigation spawned as general-purpose counts as a writer for the roster; spawn read-only work as Explore (or lease it at spawn) so the unleased-writer check does not fire

core.hooksPath runs .claude/rediacc_hooks/git from the working tree, so a writer editing a git hook makes its unfinished code live for every commit in the repo; have such a writer build in a scratch copy and swap in a finished, tested hook in one write

A writer that arms its own background monitors keeps re-notifying the lead after it reports, one empty report per expiring timer; once its work is committed, stop it with TaskStop rather than SendMessage, which resumes it

When another writer has uncommitted provider inputs in the tree, gen-docs --write folds their state into the regions and the gen-docs pre-commit refuses the commit; regenerate in the push clone at the branch tip plus only the commit's files, then copy the regenerated docs back

A writer's report of 'tests pass' does not cover lint and types: before committing writer output, run check:ci-python-lint and check:ci-python-types on the tree; on 2026-10-07 three G12 drain commits passed their module tests and failed six pre-push gates

Never pass a computed file list to a formatter without checking it is non-empty: 'ruff format $(... | sed ...)' with an empty substitution formats the WHOLE repo (2026-10-07: 28 files, 26 markdown docs rewrapped). Use 'ruff format -- <explicit paths>' or guard with [ -n "$list" ]

A mutate-then-restore control that keeps the file size and lands within the same second can leave a stale __pycache__ .pyc, so Python runs the mutant against the restored source; delete the module's .pyc (or bump mtime) after restoring before trusting the next run

Never chain '--tick ... commit:$(git rev-parse HEAD)' after a git commit with ';': when the commit is refused (doc drift, a guard), the tick still runs and records the PREVIOUS commit's sha; use '&&' or tick in a separate call after reading the new HEAD

After the watchdog cancels a run, do not 'gh run rerun --job <id>' one failed job: the carried-over cancels stay cancelled (CI Complete can never go green), downstream jobs re-run without their upstream artifacts (Shard receipts, OPS Check reds), and no watchdog covers the new attempt. Push a new run, or 'gh run rerun <run> --failed'. Measured run 37633980671 attempt 2, 2026-10-07.

loop-next ('every box ticked ... run /pr-merge') blocks a stop while the PR head's CI run is still in_progress (run 37660537647, 168/170 jobs done, failed E2E legs awaiting the watchdog's retry): /pr-merge's first precondition is CI Complete SUCCESS on the head, so the nudge should wait for a final green run (or say 'waiting on CI') instead of blocking every stop

Chain a --tick to its commit with && and read the sha from that same commit: 'git commit ... ; H=$(git log -1 ...)' ticks the PREVIOUS commit when commit-policy refuses (doc drift), which happened twice (#8d144fdc 2026-10-07, #d849a620 2026-10-08)

--review-mark fixed refuses a fix commit that does not touch the finding's anchored file even when the fix lands in the helper that line calls (2bc9b47a.1: anchored check-account-email-templates.ts:178, fixed in scripts/lib/submodule-presence.ts inCi, a18deccd3); accept a fix commit that touches a module the anchored file imports, or allow --review-mark fixed <sha> --via <path>

Tick a plan box through worklist.py --plan-investigate (BEFORE implementing) and then --plan-tick, never by editing the plan: an edited tick skips the investigation row and check:ci-plan-implementation P-A2 reds the branch (2026-10-08: 7 boxes).

Arm wl_wake.py only as a Bash run_in_background call with timeout 2400000, never with a trailing & or disown: a detached timer is invisible to the harness, and the tracked start then answers ALREADY ARMED and exits at once (2026-10-08, twice).

The stop-gate judge treated a turbo push as forbidden while the hook's own loop-next said 'batch 3/3 finished' and block_turbo_early_push admits a complete batch (d6a6e18b5): the judge prompt should read local_batch_open / batch_ready, not the generic no-push-before-batch paragraph, once the batch is complete.

CORRECTION of the previous proposal: the judge was right. The turbo batch set includes every turbo-named plan (here 5: three finished plus PLAN-cd-errors-in-ci and PLAN-retire-bash-oracles), so 'batch 3/3 finished' counts finished plans against batch_size while the set is still open; read local_batch_open, not the finished count.

Never chain --plan-tick or --review-mark after git commit in one command: the git-level commit-policy hook (gen-docs drift) can refuse the commit, HEAD stays on the previous sha, and the verb records that wrong sha (2026-10-08: B0 ticked with 6fa321424 instead of 8bca2ba93). Commit, read the new sha, then tick in a separate call.

Before committing a file a live writer was told to edit, diff it against HEAD and commit only the lead hunk: git commit -- <path> takes the whole working-tree file, so a writer in-flight edit rides along unannounced (252e5e1d1 swept W11-B common.sh removal from greenlight.cjs).

The stop judge read the session prefix '(d778be9d)' in item text as an item id and demanded work on 'the d778be9d scope gate', which is #e70faed1 already leased; the judge prompt should strip the (<session>) ownership tag before naming items, and match a decision item ticked with an ASKED: answer (#a8e94def, D8) against its implementing item (#1a4d4455) before calling it deferred.

The stop judge reads a Remaining line that names items by id only (#e70faed1, #b4e94451) as omitting those items, because it matches on item TEXT, and then orders duplicate work (a Plan agent for a gate whose patch is already delivered). Remaining lines should carry the id AND a few words of the item text, and the judge prompt should resolve #ids against the tracked-work list before calling an item missing.

The stop judge asked for a new ops-workflow regression case for B5 (8422dd2ff) although that commit added 225 lines of regression tests (test_drills_backup_roundtrip.py +83, test_drills_backup_license.py +142, each planted red), placed on the quality-pytest shard and passing (71 passed, 2026-10-09). Before demanding a regression case, the judge should read the fix commit stat for test files and the shard manifest.

The stop judge asked three times to do P-A1 box dispositions already done and recorded: it reads an item's original title ("Find whether boxes ... deadlock the first push, then close or carry each box") and not its LATEST/update text (#05829121 records the disposition: A5 closed 22c21c938, L10/L11 moved 639131c9c, M3/k3s-137/cd-errors carried as CI-only by their own box text, W7P5-a/c carried; carry 0c0c88f0b). The judge prompt should weigh the LATEST line over the title, or the session should be able to retitle an item once its question is answered.

The stop judge re-proposes work from an item TITLE (e.g. #ec63ff8c "decide (1) and (2) with deny and allow cases") after LATEST records it delivered (ggclone.patch, 31 deny cases). Feed the judge each item LATEST as the authoritative state, and treat a title clause as satisfied when LATEST names a delivered patch for it.

The stop judge demands a Plan agent for every item it labels complicated, including per-commit review-finding fixes whose finding text already states the defect and the fix shape; a writer with a control-first test and a plant is the design there. The judge should accept a writer when the item cites review findings, and ask for a Plan agent only for new designs.

The stop judge asks queued items (other plans, after-merge) to be started locally, against the one-plan-per-PR rule the stop hook itself applies ("Queued, not blocking"). The judge should read the hook own queued/not-blocking classification and not ask for queued plans to start before loop-next names them.

Chain --tick after git commit with && (or tick in a separate call): a refused commit followed by `sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD); --tick ... commit:$sha` records the previous HEAD as evidence. worklist --tick accepts any existing commit sha; it could check that the sha is newer than the item and touches the paths the item names.

The open-high-findings check blocks every stop even when each finding is already leased to a live writer building its fix (2026-10-11: 7850c0c4.1, 9849764b.1 under w1; cac47d16.1, e085085d.1 under w2). A finding whose file is owned by a leased, live writer item that names the finding id should count as in flight, like a [>] item, and the check should stand down to an advisory until the lease expires or the writer finishes.

the unleased-writer roster counts a COMPLETED subagent as a live writer started 0m ago when it re-emits a task-notification after compaction (abd69eb18c37c52f3 ran 76266831 ms and was status completed, TaskStop said 'not running (status: completed)'); judge liveness from the harness task status, not from the newest notification

the stop-gate judge reads an item's ORIGINAL text as open work and ignores its LATEST line: #bd51855a's 2026-10-13 text names turboci.patch and fd4eda1a.1-.3, both done (04072744c, 03e7af3a0) and stated in LATEST, yet five consecutive stops were refused for omitting them; it also ordered the embedpin patches applied a day early, against the item's own WHY (release-age soak until 2026-10-15T00:00Z). The judge prompt should weigh LATEST over the add text and respect a deferral's stated WHY

a [?] whose DEFAULT is time-gated (apply on or after a fixed UTC time, here the dependency release-age window) has no honest state: defer-expired fires once 120 min pass although the default cannot run yet, --lease worker:queue is refused while writer slots are free, and BLOCKED_BY needs an item id; a not-before:<ISO> field on a deferral, which holds the window until that time, would fit

A high per-commit finding already assigned to a live, leased writer still blocks every stop; the lead can only wait. Arm a background until-loop on the writer's deliverable (its .tsv) so the stop is a real wait, or teach review-block to stand down while the finding's file is owned by a verified live writer.

A deferral carrying NOT-BEFORE is not due until that instant: the stop judge called pins T13 due at 22:11Z while #c33b8946 holds NOT-BEFORE:2026-10-15T00:00Z and npm run pins -- status embed:csisnapshotter prints 'inside the window until 2026-10-15T00:00:00Z'. The judge should read the NOT-BEFORE token (wl_core.not_before_pending) before naming a held DEFAULT as the next action.

the unfixed-finding phrase check fires on a finding the same message names as tracked by a leased [>] item with a live worker (c0261286.1 under #90af5781); it should accept an id already open in the store as tracked

the stop judge orders 'write the code locally' for items whose whole content is an action that needs the push or a live run (#6361fc5b and #57f0604c are operator orders to push and /pr-babysit; #9b2100de VC0/VC6 need a VERIFIED vm:check on a grand only the operator can create; #50cb9316 needs the PR's first CI run per check-lane-budget.ts:109; #0781a2a6 waits on #50cb9316); a judge rule should read an item's BLOCKED_BY and its text before calling it locally writable

the PR-plan block holds a stop on a box whose acceptance is a post-merge event (R1: a green scheduled CI on main) while the merge itself waits on an operator-only secret; such a box should read as waiting on its merge prerequisite, not as open work this session can do

A per-commit review finding on a peer's commit (7d63b458, PR-TASK 8ed364fe, session d778be9d, live 5 minutes earlier) blocked the stop of a different session that only added a plan on the same branch; the review-finding check should block the session whose epic the commit carries, and report peers' findings instead
A read-only investigation spawned as general-purpose counts as a WRITER and needs a lease; spawn read-only fan-out as Explore (or lease an item for it at spawn time).

ci-red-unwatched fires on the old head while its fixes are committed locally and the pre-push receipt chain is running in the background; it could recognise unpushed commits newer than the red head plus a live ci:quick task as "fix in flight" rather than "nothing watching".

Arm the wake timer only with the Bash tool run_in_background flag, never with a trailing & or disown in a foreground call: an untracked timer blocks the tracked one, and this session repeated that slip twice on 2026-10-19.

A Review Complete red posted before any PR review ran (0 s, no steps, log 404) is the review aggregator waiting on the review the ready flip just started; a running wl_prreview.py --wait IS the watcher for it, so the "nothing is watching it" check should count a live wl_prreview --wait as a watch for the Review Complete context.

The stop judge keeps ordering a deferred item started locally even when the item records why it cannot start: #63840312 (B7 ubuntu-slim) was pushed three times to "write the 13 runs-on edits on a new branch", though (1) GitHub documents ubuntu-slim as 1 CPU, unprivileged container, 15-minute job timeout, so most of the 13 jobs cannot run there; (2) block_second_branch refuses a new branch; (3) the only candidates run on main/release events, so no measurement exists before the merge. The judge should read a deferred item's recorded blocker evidence (vendor limit, branch rule, missing measurement) before calling it locally startable.

turbo-next named PLAN-vm-check.md while a live non-plan writer (leased to #95980422) was editing the exact files the plan Owns; block_plan_concurrency only compares plan writers, so the pick ignored a live lease on the same files. The turbo pick should skip a plan whose Owns overlap the files of any live leased writer, not only other plan writers.

review-mark not-a-bug for a submodule finding resolves path:line and shas only inside that submodule, so evidence living in the console caller (path or sha) is refused; cite the submodule line and name the console caller in prose

a review finding anchored on a source line that reports a missing test cannot be marked fixed by a test-only commit (fixed demands the sha touch the anchored file); such findings close as not-a-bug citing the new test line, which misnames a fix

the judge read an open [?] whose DEFAULT is already implemented (box 3 committed ae57c54 under #829e486b, item #4e4c5ecc LATEST says so) as idle work and ordered it built again; a [?] whose DEFAULT is being built under the default should be shown as such (link the implementing items) so the judge does not order a duplicate

a --tick for a main hotfix the operator pushed is refused as commit-less: commit:<sha> must be reachable from the branch HEAD, and a hotfix lives on origin/main only; the tick should also accept a commit reachable from origin/main

A read-only agent prompt that merely names other item ids (#5f43e8c8 #cba857c9 #0e0e8021 as context) gets those items auto-leased to it, and they surface as leased-to-finished-worker when it ends; name context items without the # prefix, or release them after the agent reports.

ci-red kept blocking although the stop message named all three failing jobs ("Account E2E (1/4)", "E2E Workers (oracle-10, 1/8)", "E2E Backup Browse-At") in a table with their local fix shas: the job-name match likely wants the exact "Tests + Infra / <job>" spelling, or ignores table cells. A red whose fix is committed and waits only on the pre-push ci:quick should also count as watched when a background ci:quick wait is live.

The pr-review stop check reads a cached review state: after resolving a finding thread by hand (GraphQL resolveReviewThread), wl_prreview.py --check --pr 601 exited 0 and GitHub showed 0 unresolved threads, yet the hook still reported thread 4353675090 unresolved. The check should re-read (or invalidate its cache) when wl_prreview.py --answer/--check last wrote a newer verdict.

Run pytest only through .ci/cache/toolchain/uv-tools/bin/pytest from the repo root; it is a bash core-lease wrapper, so extracting its shebang interpreter runs Python files as bash (backtick spans execute), and -p no:cacheprovider fails with rc=4

An open per-commit finding whose fix item is leased to a verified live writer should stand down like a leased worklist item instead of blocking every stop; today c7dd6c1d.1 blocked while #a5269c96 (worker afcda684, live) was fixing it.
Never edit private/renet while vm:check runs: rdc.sh deploys the build of the moving tree and V1.1 then fails on a hash mismatch (2026-10-24, vmc-10232255-dedd88).

A mutating ./rdc.sh verb (repo fork/up/down/delete, sync upload, machine setup) against a production machine uploads THIS checkout renet; hostinger runs old renet 7e6a8588 and the branch renet changes the runtime layout, so a fork on hostinger from this branch migrates production (#d0928775). Use read-only verbs there until the planned upgrade.

A judge timeout under heavy load is load starvation, not an unreachable model: on 2026-10-24 one of 589 judge calls timed out (14:50Z) while ci:quick drove load average to ~200 for 3757s wall; STOPHOOK_CHILD=1 claude -p reply OK answered in 2.3s (8.3s wall) at that load. Check uptime and a running ci:quick or vm:check before touching the gate; the next stop retries the judge, and WORKLIST_JUDGE=off is never the answer to one timeout.

plan-tick CLAUSE 1 has no honest door for work a writer landed before the lead investigated: --retro reaches only ticked boxes and --plan-tick refuses without a row, so the lead ends up citing a submodule sha the ancestry check cannot see. Either investigate each box before spawning its writer, or add a --late flag that records the implementing commit and is counted like --retro.

The open-review-finding block fires even when the fix is already assigned to a verifiably live writer whose item names the finding (7bfbc416.1 on #e10c87d5, d722e0bf.2 on #e911e018), so every stop while those writers run is refused with nothing the lead can do; a finding named by an open item leased to a live worker should stand down like CAP-SATURATED WAIT until that worker reports.

During an operator /hibernate (start nothing new, wait for running work, then shutdown.exe /h) the stop judge still orders new local work (here wave 3 #e05ccbaa) and refuses the stop; a hibernate in progress should stand the judge down like a wind-down phase, keeping only the floor and the waits on running tasks.

A judge timeout while the API is slow is environmental, not a gate bug: on 2026-10-26 a bare STOPHOOK_CHILD=1 claude -p 'reply OK' took 61s (3.9s normally) with ci:quick and six agents loading the machine, so the 240s budget (capped by the harness hook kill, wl_judge.py:43-47) could not fit the schema-bound call. Measure the bare call first; if it is 10x slow, retry the stop once load drops rather than raising the timeout or disabling the judge

When Claude Code reaps a background run for low system memory (task status killed, "running low on memory"), do not restart it or spawn heavy writers; report it, record the stop on the item, and wait for the operator, because restarting under the same pressure gets reaped again and the hook pushing for the next box does not free memory.

A server-side refusal change (a new 4xx on an existing route) is verified against the whole account suite (npm run check:ci-account-server) and a grep of every client of that route, portal included, never only the one test file the change touched; R1 clean break passed config-envelope-v3.test.ts and broke 8 config-sync tests and the portal

Write a verification rc into a commit message only after reading that exact run's output; a check that moved to the background has no rc yet, and committing before reading it records a claim, not a result (feb0c5db4 claimed prose rc=0 while the run printed prose=1)

A new .ci file cannot be committed alone while other .ci paths are uncommitted: the gen-docs pre-commit derives doc-registry and port-brief counts from the commit tree, and gen-docs --write reads the working tree, so the two never match; batch the .ci commits and run gen-docs --write once over the whole set

An agent that ended its turn with its own background Bash timer running is still working (the harness resumes it when the timer exits); the leased-to-finished-worker check reads it as dead because a sub-agent's background shell is not counted as a live descendant. Count the agent's background tasks, or accept the agent's 'waiting on its own background work' status, before calling the lease dead.

a --plan-investigate fileline pointer names the changed line (from git diff), never :1, and a submodule change cites the submodule commit in the note beside the console pointer commit; the per-commit review flags :1 pointers every time

plan-concurrency judges a live agent by its plan header Owns, so a live-proof agent whose brief edits only the plan file and /tmp (L1 on hostinger) is flagged against a code writer of another plan sharing a header glob; a live-only agent should be spawned without the Plan:/Owns: header, or the check should read the brief Owns line instead of the plan header

A read-only investigator brief that lets an agent read ~/.config/rediacc/*.json must forbid printing config values: use key-only jq paths (keys, has, length, type) and never select a repo or machine object whole, because those objects carry credentials and SSH private keys. On 2026-10-29 one broad jq filter printed a production LUKS credential and repo SSH key into tool output.

block_plan_concurrency is blind to writers spawned in the same message: five overlapping writers all passed the spawn guard because none was live yet when the others were checked; spawn overlapping-risk writers one message at a time, or the guard should also check sibling calls of the same batch

The open-review-finding check should stand down (advise, not block) when the finding is named in an open item leased to a verified-live writer that owns the anchored file: a16a7407.1 (pkg/chunkstore/pipeline_linux.go) is in #b2464b5c leased to worker a736b649f6ed8d218, and the lead editing that file mid-writer would corrupt it; the block then repeats every stop with nothing to do

A triaged PLAN+SUBAGENT item carries the slug the judge chose; write the plan under exactly that path (worklist --list shows it), or the concurrency guard reads the missing plan as Owns ** and refuses every other writer

While npm run ci:quick runs for a push receipt, HEAD must not move: the receipt is refused with 'HEAD moved while these gates ran' (seen this session), so committing other work during the run wastes it; a stop that waits on ci:quick with no commits is legitimate, and items that need the pushed branch (preview smoke, vm:check, live runs) are not local work

The PR-plan block names the next open box even when the worklist item that carries that box is deferred [?] to the operator with a WHY that the box needs a PR the operator declined (PLAN-backup-program 695c3218 under #ab9c68b1, 2026-10-31T07:3xZ); it should skip a box whose carrying item is an operator-deferred [?] and name the next one, or stand down when every open box is behind such a deferral, live proof or the merge.

The stop judge re-demands local work for items whose LATEST already says NO LOCAL HALF with the closing condition (a nightly, vm:check, a post-push run), every stop while a CI run is the real wait; it should read the NO LOCAL HALF marker as evidence instead of asking the session to re-prove it each stop, which burns turns on a 93%-used weekly budget (2026-10-31).

/hibernate step 1 forbids new background jobs and step 2 lets the wake timer be stopped, yet the wake-timer FLOOR blocks the stop that waits on the remaining task; /hibernate should exempt the wake timer from step 1, or the floor should stand down while a hibernate is pending

A live peer session's sub-agent reports block a different session's stop: wl_report.unread filters by branch and drops only foreign reports that are stale (_foreign_and_stale), so 45048a90's writers' reports demanded reading from d778be9d, a resumed session that never spawned them. Reports of a live foreign session belong to that session and should be reported, not blocking.

A session the operator /exit-ed still reads as LIVE: its background pty process survives with its wake timer and CI wait, and the harness writes an away_summary and a lastevent afterwards, so --migrate refuses and a resumed predecessor concludes a peer is running. Check the transcript for /exit before calling a session live.

The stop check "CI IS RED AND NOTHING IS WATCHING" fires on a final run when the fix is committed and a live pre-push chain (ci:quick, vm:check) is the only thing between it and the push. A final run has nothing to watch; a background pre-push run on unpushed commits ahead of the red head should stand it down.

The stop-gate judge ordered git worktree add, which CLAUDE.md and block_worktree_add reserve for the operator, and earlier ordered a hand rewrite of the append-only plan-investigation ledger. A judge next action must be checked against the guards and the ledger rules before it is proposed; a live receipt run on a verified tree is a legitimate reason to hold local edits.

The judge kept ordering a worktree or scratch copy after the operator ruled on 2026-11-04 that /tmp clones are to be refused and git worktree add stays guarded until the lease tool lands. It should read rulings newer than the guard text.

The stop-gate judge told a session to drop a backup push as forbidden under turbo batch-end, while the same hook printed BACKUP PUSH DUE and the operator had kept it in ASKED:2026-11-04T17:3xZ. The backup_push_h valve admits that push, so the judge prompt should read it as allowed.
A lease tree whose dirty files were superseded by landed commits cannot be collected by gc, which keeps every dirty tree and offers no discard: remove the stale copies, then gc --write --id

plan-concurrency judges a coordinator agent by its Plan line alone: a coordinator that declares Owns none and spawns only leased writers still counts as claiming the whole plan Owns, so it trips against a main-checkout writer on an overlapping file; judge a writer by the Owns line of its brief when present

review-mark fixed refuses a fix that lands only in the anchor's test (e.g. test_core_run_verbs.py for run_verbs.py) unless --test <path> is passed, and its refusal says no touched test carries the stem although one does; pass --test, or make the refusal name --test

bg-orphan flags a server a finished sub-agent launched (here ./run.sh account dev on :4800) even when a live background run of the lead depends on it (suite 32 case 5 needs the gateway); killing it fails that run. Exempt a process whose port a live lead task is using, or one named in a leased item (here #8bb9e583, 'kill after bbjioayw3 exits'); the lead kills it when the dependent task ends

unlanded-lease blocks a stop while a vm:check runs, but landing a CLI or renet commit mid-run changes the tree vm:check rebuilds from per rdc call (run 1 of 2026-11-06 failed V1.1 for exactly that); the check should stand down while a vm:check of this session is live and the lease items are leased worker:lead with that reason

the stop judge repeatedly orders work on "queued review fixes" from /tmp/findings-account.tsv and similar files that a previous context created and that no longer exist; every open id is in the worklist guide, and a judge claim about queued work should be checked against the guide and the files on disk before it blocks a stop

the stop judge ordered new turbo-batch work three times after the operator explicitly asked the session to pause until a Claude Code update (2026-11-06 ~06:45Z); a live operator pause must stand the judge down to wait-only, with the running task and the wake timer as the whole roster

unlanded-lease blocks while ci:quick runs on the live tree; landing then moves HEAD and voids the receipt the push needs. Like the vm:check fleet-lock stand-down (cc0a9ef9), a running ci:quick (its lock or a live npm run ci:quick task) should turn the block into a report until it exits.

a live drill on a production machine that forks/deletes repos must not run inside the machine's scheduled backup window (hostinger nightly-hot 02:00Z): on 2026-11-06 a fork deleted at 02:01Z failed the nightly. Check the machine's backup timers before a mutating hostinger run.

do not start writers while ci:quick runs: on 2026-11-06 six lease writers (vitest, go test, pytest) beside ci:quick drove load to 260 on 24 cores and check:ci-pytest timed out at 4937s (limit 4591s), a false red that costs a full rerun. Order: land, then ci:quick alone, then the next writer wave.

before landing a lease, check git -C <lease> status for untracked files: on 2026-11-06 a writer committed c79f9174a with 'git commit -- <paths>' but never 'git add'ed its new test file, so the landed fix had no test until gc's rule 3 kept the tree. './run.sh worktree land' could print untracked paths beside the cherry-pick lines.

the impossible-claim check fires on a negated mention: 'I haven't claimed anything can't be done' and 'claimed dismissed' tripped it twice in a row on 2026-11-06; it should skip a match inside a negation (haven't/not/no ... can't) or quoted reference to the check itself.

Parse new ids from --add/--add-many with the 'added #<id>' prefix only: a 'WARNING: similar open item: #<id>' line in the same output shifted a grep -o '#[0-9a-f]*' list by one, and six leases and ticks landed on the wrong items (2026-11-06).

Before `cat > path` for a new file, test that the path does not exist: on 2026-11-06 a "new" non-Linux stub overwrote the tracked repository_maintain_other.go (it already held createMaintainCmd); the repair was a forward rewrite of the original plus the addition. Name new files after checking `ls`/`git ls-files`, or use the Write tool, which refuses an unread existing file.

The review-finding wait stand-down matches finding ids only in a leased item TEXT, written in full (94332990.2), not a range like 94332990.1-.3 and not an --update note; name every high id in the --add text of the item leased to the fixing writer.

The stop-gate judge ordered the ops repo target file committed to the console tree, but PLAN-health-checks-local ruling A keeps the operator hosts out of the public tree (the file lives only in the ops repo on hostinger, deploy_ops_health docstring), and H9 was already leased to a live runner (#a3c2628a); it also read the heartbeat cron as 02:17Z while CronList showed the next run at 02:39 local = 01:39Z. A judge next-action that commits infrastructure data to a public repo, or that duplicates a leased item, is refused with this citation.

A survey sub-agent reported PLAN-token-ip-rebind T9 as ccc8c7a8 while wl_planrec.open_boxes gives ccc8658a; --plan-investigate with the wrong sig prints "Nothing was written" and nothing else. Read every box sig from the parser right before --plan-investigate, never from a survey report, and treat "Nothing was written" as a wrong-sig signal.

CORRECTION to the previous plan-tick hint: --plan-investigate exits 2 and prints its reason on the line above "Nothing was written."; the earlier call hid it behind tail -1. Read the whole output and the exit code of a plan verb; never tail -1 it.
The stop judge reads an item original finding text as still-open work; when sub-findings are fixed, put a STATUS PER FINDING line in --update so the LATEST names each one done with its sha

Landing lease commits that add CLI verbs or options leaves three generated artifacts that lease writers skip: the CLI hash manifest (npm run i18n:generate-hashes), the CLI reference pages (npm run generate:cli-docs -w @rediacc/www, 13 locales) and the job-plan coverage registry (JOB_PLANS or JOB_EXCEPTIONS in packages/cli/src/services/jobs/plans.ts). Run all three after landing and before ci:quick

The stop judge re-asks for local code work on every stop while a fleet run is live even after a survey (/tmp/g5_boxes.txt) found none; it should read an item LATEST line that names the survey result and stand down instead of re-ordering the same check

A redundant change committed in a lease after the same change landed on the branch inside a larger commit stays unlanded forever (patch-id and -x both miss); gc has --discard-dirty for redundant uncommitted paths but no waiver for a redundant commit; prefer --discard-dirty over committing in the lease, or land the lease commit with git cherry-pick -x --keep-redundant-commits

An item whose code is written and committed in a lease but held for landing behind a fleet run reads to the stop judge as unstarted work when its LATEST says only "land after"; write "FIXED, NOTHING LEFT TO WRITE: <lease shas>; only the cherry-pick remains" so the judge does not order a duplicate writer

worklist.py --add folds a new item into an existing open one when the texts overlap (three round-2 writer items became #235d49d7, and a fourth was merged into the unrelated #eb5c1323); read the id --add prints and give parallel items clearly distinct wording before leasing

Do not commit anything (agent/ plans and review records included) while ./run.sh drill backup and drill backup-onprem run before vm:check: the backup-check receipt is keyed on the tree, so a commit between the two drills starts a new receipt with no legs and vm:check stops at receipt-first (fleet run 15, 2026-11-07, tree ccb4a5a1 then 0cce58a0); commit after vm:check has started

Keep the host idle while a fleet run executes its external legs: suite 31 backup-large-2g has a time budget of 10% of its seed (about 10.8 s), and three review writers running tests beside fleet run 15b pushed the incremental to 12.9 s and turned the run red; start writers before or after the fleet run, not during

The stop judge asks to tick P-A1 boxes with on-disk evidence, but every open box of the three preflight plans got an investigation row at 15:0xZ (9bbeedb6e): all are partial or absent live runs, so none is tickable from code; the judge should read the newest investigation rows before calling the batch idle

When a [>] item loses its worker and cannot run yet, the fix is --lease <me> <id> release <note>, not --update (keeps the dead worker) or worker:queue (refused while writer slots are free); the dead-worker message should print the release verb

A BLOCKED_BY:#id written in a --lease <id> release note is not read as a dependency (the item lists as plain open); only an --update note sets it, so a release of blocked work is followed by --update with BLOCKED_BY

plan-unimplemented says nothing of this session is running for the PR plan while fleet run 16 (task bf4u5yqf1, leased on #11306719) is the very run every remaining box waits on; the check should count a live leased background task whose item the plan boxes are blocked by, instead of naming the next box (A1a, a preview smoke that needs a CI preview deploy)

A per-commit review finding whose fix is owned by a live leased writer (here 1a984268.1 and f6cf1731.1, both fixed by X1 #62c91192 in check_proxy_deploy_dry_run.py and ci_workflow_invariants.py) still blocks every stop; the lead cannot fix the file without racing the writer. The check could stand down while an open item naming the finding id is leased to a verified live worker, and fire again when that worker ends.

The pr-plan-set block re-fires every stop when every open box is gated on an operator [?] deferral (here #1b86eb2f: a ci:quick the harness reaped for memory and reserved for the operator) or on the push, CI or a VERIFIED vm:check that deferral unlocks; it should stand down, like CAP-SATURATED WAIT, when the plan sets remaining boxes all trace to an open [?] of this session, and name that [?] instead of the next box

The stop-gate judge ordered a [?] DEFAULT executed 11 minutes into its 120-minute window (#c786ce9f, P13) and named a correction stamped ASKED:<minute>Z, which only an operator answer can supply; a DEFAULT runs when its window closes (the hook already orders it then), and a correction made by a DEFAULT is labelled by the deferral id, never ASKED. An open deferral window is a legitimate wait, not idle local work

A live runner briefed 'Owns: none' becomes a holder of its plan's whole Owns the moment it edits one file (even its own plan file), so two runners on plans with overlapping Owns globs (rename .ci/rediacc_ci/ops/** vs website apply_cf_redirect_rules.py) trip PLAN CONCURRENCY BROKEN although each touches disjoint files. Before spawning parallel runners, name in each brief the files the other runner owns and forbid them; the concurrency check should judge a runner's ACTUAL edited paths, not its plan's globs.

The stop-gate judge re-orders "advance the turbo batch boxes locally" every stop while a ci:quick runs, even after the session listed every open batch box with its ledger verdict (all live, CI-run or post-push). A local commit then would void the running receipt (record-paths). The judge should read plan-investigation.jsonl verdicts and the running ci:quick lease before ordering local box work, and accept a box table already given this context.

When a box survey classified every open box of the PR plan set as live, CI, pipeline or operator work (0 G5), the stop-gate judge should accept a named vm:check or fleet wait without demanding local box work; also no code writer may run beside vm:check on its inputs. Evidence: survey /tmp/writers-now/1104-1-20261110T0528Z.md, PR plan set 21 open boxes 0 G5, judge demanded local batch work 6 times on 2026-11-10.

While vm:check runs on the head tree, a local commit voids the receipt it is producing; a batch whose remaining boxes are all live halves gated on that receipt has no local work, and the stop judge should read the vm:check lease as covering them.

Lease writers report ruff format clean, yet the gate (ruff 0.17.4, format --no-cache) finds their files unformatted after landing: six files in one wave on 2026-11-10. A writer brief should name the exact gate command `ruff format --no-cache` and `npm run check:ci-python-lint` as the accept, not a bare ruff format.

stop-gate judge counts a box as local work when its latest plan-investigation row is partial with --owed live/ci/post-push (box-audit shows live-owed); it repeatedly orders writers for A4d 0a237b2e, J6 575e0098, J9 07955f58 whose code landed and whose Accept is a CI run id. The judge input should carry box-audit live-owed state and drop those boxes from the local count.

review-mark fixed refuses a fix that lands in the callee of the anchored line (cd64926e.1: subscription-repo-table.ts:12 calls outputService.report; the fix is report() in services/core/output.ts, 6d47b5720e), so a correct callee fix can only be recorded as not-a-bug; --review-mark fixed should accept a commit that touches a function the anchored line calls, or a --callee <path:line> form

block_hand_review_write misses a python heredoc that finds review paths with a subprocess grep -l and writes them (2026-11-10: the AKIA redaction script edited agent/reviews/1104-1/09cc0984...md and broke its Body-Sig unrefused); the guard should catch any python write whose target resolves under agent/reviews, however the path is built

never filter ./run.sh worktree land output through grep cherry-pick: land prints the git add and git commit -F <msg> -- <sub> gitlink lines between the picks, and the filter hid them on 2026-11-10, so the account pointer drifted and vm:check refused on checkout-mismatch; run the printed lines whole

this host tail is uutils coreutils 0.10.0: the short form tail -N rejects several file arguments ("error: unexpected argument -2"), measured 2026-11-10 by the lead and the K3.3 runner; always write tail -n N

the open-review-finding block fires even when an open item leased to a live writer names the finding and the fix is in flight (2026-11-10, b3ef7ca3.1 on #8638dd20); a finding carried by a live lease should stand down to an advisory until the lease ends, the way plan boxes with a live worker do

the stop-gate judge ordered AskUserQuestion while away mode was set (2026-11-10T23:0xZ, item #20d0b3ea); block_away_questions refuses the ask, and the away procedure is exactly a parked [?] with DEFAULT. The judge input should carry the away flag and accept a parked deferral as the legitimate state of an operator-only item

during a conflicted cherry-pick of a guard change, the guard file in the working tree is the incoming version and is already live in the hooks; on 2026-11-11 it refused a python heredoc that only edited the test file, and the same command passed (rc 0) through dispatch once the pick finished; resolve guard-file conflicts with the Edit tool, never a scripted Bash write

A run duration read from a log file mtime or a local-time run id is CET, not UTC: read startedAt/finishedAt/wallMs from the receipt instead (2026-11-11: vm:check reported as 90 min, really 30.2; the 4th CET-as-Z slip after 2026-11-08)

Before telling the operator a CI rerun cannot pick up a fix (title, body, labels), read the step source: .ci/scripts/ci/validate-pr.cjs reads the PR title live, so gh run rerun --failed works after a retitle (2026-11-11: claimed a push was needed)

A sub-agent waiting for a fixed clock instant more than 20 minutes away (a cron proof point) trips the stale-waiter kill if it uses an until/sleep loop; brief live runners to wait with the Monitor tool or chained waits of 15 minutes or less, and the check could exempt a loop whose target instant is still in the future.

Never run a --lease loop with a stand-in worker id (worker:PLACEHOLDER) even with output suppressed: the store is append-only, so each call writes a lease that names a worker that never existed; lease only after the background task returns its real id, and supersede any stand-in at once with the real id.

A STATE.md hand-over commit is not record-only (.ci/policy/record-paths.json covers reviews, worklist, reggate, effort ledgers and carried-reds only), so committing it between a green ci:quick and the push voids the receipt; write and commit STATE.md before the gate run, or after the push.

worktree gc has no way to drop a lease whose only unlanded commit is a proven duplicate: lease agent-a15587079924dd0ed holds 9ad740120a (same test fix as landed 3e517f65b3; its cherry-pick conflicts on the same lines, skipped) and `gc --write --id <id> --discard-dirty <reason>` still keeps it (rule: unlanded commit), so the UNLANDED LEASE stop check fires forever. Add a --superseded-by <sha> waiver to gc (and to the stop check) that records the landed equivalent.

wl_review --review-mark fixed <sha> --test <t> refuses when the named test reads a data file (en.json) rather than importing a module: related_test matches by name and imports_anchored_module by import, so a test that loads the anchored JSON is never related (6a049fc8.1, legal-meta.test.ts). Treat a test whose added lines name the anchored file basename as related.

wl_review --review-mark fixed refuses a fix that edits the file the finding says was left out (cbe1ba5b.1 anchored at .devcontainer/toolchain.env, fixed by 0b9b783903 in package.json): the relatedness check only accepts the anchored file, its moves or tests. A finding whose claim names another path ("leaves X at ...") should accept a fix touching that path; until then such findings get recorded as not-a-bug with the fix sha, which mislabels them.

block_review_file_shell_write refuses `./rdc.sh --config eu-bench term connect hostinger -c "sudo renet list all --json > /tmp/rl.json; ..."` as "writes a per-commit review record by hand": a redirect to /tmp/rl.json inside a remote -c string is neither a local write nor a review path. The guard should resolve the redirect target and only refuse writes under agent/reviews/.

wl_planrec --plan-investigate fileline pointers reject a path with no extension (packages/cli/templates/elite/Rediaccfile:1 -> "carries no <path>:<line> citation"); extensionless tracked files such as Rediaccfile, Dockerfile and Makefile should resolve as file:line pointers.

writers-now step 3 says a wave waits while uptime load exceeds nproc, but --lease worker:queue refuses any reason except a full writer cap ("worker:queue is only for writer work the cap forbids starting"), so a load-held writer has no lease form and the open item trips the stop hook; give --lease a load-hold note (worker:queue load:<x>/<nproc>) or drop the load rule

worktree land --ticks prints a ready --plan-investigate line with commit:<submodule sha> for a submodule landing, and --plan-investigate refuses it ("commit FAIL no such commit") because it resolves commits only in the console repo; land --ticks should cite the console gitlink commit, or the commit kind should resolve inside the submodule the fileline names

review-mark fixed refuses when the fix is in a different file than the finding (d3df33c3.1: map entry red at bws-secret-map.json, fixed by the call-site commit fe467f3f touching secret-supply.json); --test accepts only test paths, so a gate script cannot be named; a fix-in-sibling-file case needs a --via <path> or cross-commit form instead of forcing not-a-bug

a writer that waits on its own npm run ci -- --narrow with `until ! pgrep -f "npm run [c]i"` also waits on any other session or lead ci:quick run on the host, so the loop outlives its purpose (pid 2927513 ran 20+ min after the narrow run it watched); writer briefs should say: run the narrow set in the foreground or as a background task and wait for its notification, never a pgrep loop

push-gated items (a dozen riding one push) must be re-leased every time the writer they were leased to finishes, because a lease names one worker; three re-lease rounds this context for the same 12 items. A lease form naming a set of workers (worker:a,b,c, live while any is) or naming the push itself (worker:push:<branch>) would hold them until the push lands
